messages:
maria (support): Hey team, customer 'ClientCo' opened an escalation — their streaming responses are frequently cutting off mid-output and clients see a 1006 close. They say it happens after ~30s of inactivity. Repro steps included a long generation that sometimes returns partial tokens then disconnects. 

client-ops: We hit them back for logs, but they sent a minimal repro: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=long-gen\"` then wait ~30s, stream stops, TCP RST or websocket 1006 on browser. No obvious 500. 

kevin (sre): thanks. Do they use our hosted gateway or behind some proxy? any LB in front?

client-ops: Hosted (us-east). They mentioned corporate firewall and nginx reverse proxy on their side, but also we route through our edge + cloud LB.

ryan (eng-runtime): 1006 usually means abnormal closure (client or network). If they're behind nginx with no SSE keepalive, idle TCP can be killed. Also some CDNs have 30s idle connection timeouts.

maria (support): They also reported partial outputs on reconnect — sometimes new connection resumes but newer tokens are duplicated or missing. They asked about 'resume' semantics.

olivia (pm): Is there a safe resume token? We don't support true resume mid-generation today, only re-issuing a request with same prompt and offset. Need to set expectations.

ryan (eng-runtime): Correct. For streaming we don't support resurrecting an interrupted in-flight generation. We can support idempotent resume by returning an idempotency token for completed chunks, but that's not implemented. For now we should prevent idle disconnects.

kevin (sre): Quick triage plan: (1) check edge LB idle timeout and upstream keepalive. (2) confirm our SSE comment ping behavior (do we send ':' comment every 15s?). (3) ask client to test with curl + `--no-buffer` and to run a direct curl to our edge (bypass their nginx) if possible.

maria (support): Client tried `--no-buffer`. They say bypassing their nginx helps sometimes. They also attached a HAR showing their browser reconnect logic triggers after 28s.

deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-12T18:02:11Z finished (edge-keepalive: enabled).

kevin (sre): I pulled edge config — we emit a 15s comment ping in hosted api for SSE (line starting with `: ping\n\n`). But there's an extra proxy in their path that strips comment lines (some middleboxes consider `:` lines malformed) and so nothing reaches client and intermediate LB thinks connection is idle. Oof.

ryan (eng-runtime): Two approaches: 1) Use ``
: ping

`` comment keepalive (safe per SSE spec) OR 2) emit a tiny JSON chunk like `{"keepalive":true}` as an actual event — but that complicates client parsing. Also TCP keepalive at OS level can help but won't prevent app-layer timeouts from proxies.

maria (support): Client asks if we can switch to TCP-level keepalive or adjust edge to send more frequent frames.

kevin (sre): We can lower comment ping to 10s on edge for a canary for this tenant. But we need to confirm it won't affect billing/metrics. Also need to monitor for middleboxes that drop streams when data comes too frequently.

ryan (eng-runtime): Alternatively, send a `: ` comment plus a small `data: \"\n\n\"` event? Example SSE output chunk we currently use: 
```
data: {"id":"abc","choice":"token","text":"hello"}

: ping

```
If proxies strip leading `:` then we could send `event: keepalive
data: ""

` as a real event the client ignores. That will be robust but adds application-visible events.

client-ops: Would client parsing break? They use EventSource in browser that ignores unknown events by default, but some SDKs might treat it differently.

olivia (pm): Need to be explicit in docs if we add `event: keepalive`. Also we should offer a config flag per-tenant.

maria (support): Action items for now: (A) ask client to test bypassing their nginx (done), (B) enable 10s comment ping canary for their tenant on hosted edge, (C) provide sample repro curl + expected behavior, (D) draft docs on keepalive/resume semantics.

kevin (sre): I'll flip the canary for tenant_id=clientco-42 on the edge. I'll also add extra tracing to log the last-send timestamp per connection (for 24h).

ryan (eng-runtime): For the curl repro, share this command: 
```
# reproduce streaming, show raw frames and keepalive comments
curl -v -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=long-gen&stream=true\" \
| sed -n '1,200p' 
```
We expect to see SSE `data:` lines followed by `: ping` comment lines every 10-15s. If the comments are missing, the intermediate dropped them.

client-ops: Client tried a version that shows comments missing when they go through their corp proxy. When they connect directly to our edge (they were able to from a VM in their cloud), comments are present and stream stays alive.

maria (support): So strong likelihood it's their proxy dropping comment pings which causes connection to appear idle and get killed. For partial outputs on reconnect: explain we don't resume mid-generation; they can re-run request but need to dedupe on client side.

olivia (pm): Let's prepare two follow-ups: (1) recommend if they control proxy to allow SSE comments or increase idle timeouts, (2) enable keepalive-event canary for them and return to confirm. Also include client-side guidance for fallback: on reconnect, check last tokens and request with same prompt + offset or use dedupe.

kevin (sre): Canary enabled for clientco-42 at 1789200300. Edge logs show keepalive events emitted. I'll monitor for disconnect rate over next 24h.

maria (support): Messaging to client (draft): 
- We found likely cause: corporate proxy stripping SSE comment keepalives, causing idle close (~30s). 
- Short-term options: bypass proxy, configure proxy to allow SSE or increase idle timeout, or we can enable a per-tenant keepalive event (we enabled canary). 
- We do not support resuming an in-flight generation; if a stream aborts, re-issue the request and dedupe on client-side. 

client-ops: Client confirmed they saw improved behavior with the canary — fewer disconnects in their VM-to-edge tests. They're testing from users behind the proxy next. :thumbsup:

maria (support): Great. I will close the escalation after 48h if metrics hold. Thanks all. :slightly_smiling_face:

kevin (sre): Logging note: include `last_sent_ms` in connection trace so we can rule out edge-side inactivity quickly in future.

ryan (eng-runtime): Long term: consider offering official `keepalive_mode` options in API: `comment`, `event`, `tcp` and document tradeoffs. Filing a ticket.

maria (support): Filed support ticket SUP-2026-321. Closing loop with client in 48h.

deploy-bot: canary toggle for tenant clientco-42 set to ON at 1789200300

kevin (sre): +monitoring dashboards: created `streams/keepalive/drops` chart, alert if drop-rate > 1% for a tenant.

maria (support): Thanks everyone — leaving thread open for a bit while client finishes testing.
